name: Nathan Kallus
position: Postdoctoral Associate, Operations Research and Statistics group
evidenceNote: Dimitris Bertsimas's MIT group page lists Nathan Kallus among its graduated postdoctoral students for 2015-2016. The MIT DSpace record dates his Ph.D. thesis (advisor Bertsimas, Operations Research Center) 2015, and the Cornell Tech profile says that before Cornell he was a postdoctoral associate in MIT's Operations Research and Statistics group and also a visiting scholar at USC's Department of Data Sciences and Operations. The USC visit is undated; since the MIT postdoc began in the degree year, it is recorded as the first post-PhD job. Verifier: kept. The Cornell ORIE profile (also opened) repeats that before Cornell he was a visiting scholar at USC's Department of Data Sciences and Operations and a postdoctoral associate at MIT, still without dates; the MIT DSpace record of the 2015 thesis was accessioned on 17 September 2015. No opened source dates the USC visit, so nothing shows it began between the 2015 degree and the MIT postdoc that the advisor's page dates from 2015; the Cornell wording places the USC visit immediately before Cornell.
reason: Second pass: following the triage step, the advisor's MIT group page (dbertsim.mit.edu/students, plain curl) dates the MIT postdoc 2015-2016, the year of the 2015 MIT thesis (DSpace). The USC visiting-scholar post named on the Cornell Tech profile carries no date and is taken to fall within or after the postdoc; a verifier should confirm it did not precede the postdoc in 2015. Bertsimas's CV PDF (dbertsim.mit.edu/pdfs/cv.pdf) returns 404.
